constraints: Departments need folder-level grouping and policy boundaries.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A Resource Manager folder has an organization or another folder as its parent. Projects contain service resources; they do not contain Resource Manager folders. Linking projects to a billing account does not make that account a folder parent.
details.scenarioApplication: The company has no organization resource for its requested domain-managed hierarchy. Cloud Identity or Google Workspace provides that organization context; after it exists, the company can create department folders beneath it.
details.errorCorrection: Enabling an API gives access to operations, but does not supply the missing parent. Likewise, project ownership and a billing relationship cannot replace the organization hierarchy.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Once the organization exists, folder creation also requires Folder Creator or Folder Admin at the intended parent. If an organization already exists but is not visible to the user, check access before creating another identity tenancy.
details.transfer: When a scenario changes from projects linked by billing to resources grouped by department policy, check their actual ancestry. A payment link is not a substitute for an organization or folder parent.

messages.text: A billing account pays for linked projects; it is not a Resource Manager folder parent. Department folders need an organization or another folder above them.
A project contains service resources and may sit below a folder. Making it a folder parent reverses that hierarchy; Project Owner permissions do not change the allowed parent type.
API enablement does not create the missing organization parent. A folder creation request still needs a valid organization or folder parent and the appropriate permission there.

feedback.reason: Department folders need an organization hierarchy. For this domain-managed setup, establish the organization through Cloud Identity or Google Workspace before creating folders.
